body:
The demo repo is the fleet's sandbox, and today nothing in it says when it was last used or by which run — a person opening it cannot tell a live sandbox from an abandoned one. This card adds the first of the three places that answer, and the one a reader meets first: a `## Last exercised` section in `README.md` holding exactly one stamp line between two marker comments, so the script a sibling card adds can rewrite that line in place without touching the rest of the file.

Seed the stamp with the UTC date the change is committed and this card's own identifier as the label — that is true on the day it is written, and every later exercise overwrites it. Add one sentence under the heading saying the line is rewritten by the `exercised.sh` script.

Do not create the `exercised.sh` script and do not create or edit `CHANGELOG.md` — two sibling cards own those files, and this card must leave them alone.

**Files: **`README.md`

## Contract — the exercise stamp

Written identically in this card, in the `CHANGELOG.md` card, and in the
`exercised.sh` card. One line format, spelled the same way everywhere:

```
Last exercised: <DATE> by <WHAT>
```

* `<DATE>` — the UTC calendar date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-09-04`).
* `<WHAT>` — a short single-line label naming what exercised the repo: a Linear
  card id such as `DRE-3019`, a workflow name, or the word `manual`.

Three marker comments, each on its own line, spelled exactly:

```
<!-- exercised:begin -->
<!-- exercised:end -->
<!-- exercised:log -->
```

* `README.md` holds exactly ONE stamp line, alone between `<!-- exercised:begin -->`
  and `<!-- exercised:end -->`.
* `CHANGELOG.md` holds the history: every entry is `- ` followed by the same
  stamp line, appended below `<!-- exercised:log -->`, oldest first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `README.md` carries a `## Last exercised` section containing `<!-- exercised:begin -->` and `<!-- exercised:end -->`, each on its own line, with exactly one line between them.
- [ ] That line matches the contract format exactly — `Last exercised: <YYYY-MM-DD> by <label>` — seeded with the UTC date of the commit and this card's own identifier as the label.
- [ ] One sentence under the heading says the line is rewritten by the `exercised.sh` script.
- [ ] The pull request changes `README.md` and no other file.
- [ ] `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass on the branch.

The README stamp says when the repo was last exercised; it cannot say how often, or whether the last three runs were this week or last spring. This card adds the history: a `CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root whose entries are the same stamp line, one per exercise, oldest first, appended below a marker the script a sibling card adds can find.

Create the file with a title, one sentence saying what it records and that entries are appended by the `exercised.sh` script a sibling card adds, the `<!-- exercised:log -->` marker, and one seed entry dated the UTC day of the commit with this card's own identifier as the label.

Do not create the `exercised.sh` script and do not edit `README.md` — two sibling cards own those files, and this card must leave them alone. The README card and this one are independent — they touch different files, can build at the same time, and share only the line format written out below.

**Files: **`CHANGELOG.md`

## Contract — the exercise stamp

Written identically in this card, in the `README.md` card, and in the
`exercised.sh` card. One line format, spelled the same way everywhere:

```
Last exercised: <DATE> by <WHAT>
```

* `<DATE>` — the UTC calendar date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-09-04`).
* `<WHAT>` — a short single-line label naming what exercised the repo: a Linear
  card id such as `DRE-3019`, a workflow name, or the word `manual`.

Three marker comments, each on its own line, spelled exactly:

```
<!-- exercised:begin -->
<!-- exercised:end -->
<!-- exercised:log -->
```

* `README.md` holds exactly ONE stamp line, alone between `<!-- exercised:begin -->`
  and `<!-- exercised:end -->`.
* `CHANGELOG.md` holds the history: every entry is `- ` followed by the same
  stamp line, appended below `<!-- exercised:log -->`, oldest first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` exists at the repo root and carries `<!-- exercised:log -->` on its own line.
- [ ] Below that marker there is exactly one entry: `- ` followed by a line matching the contract format, dated the UTC day of the commit with this card's own identifier as the label.
- [ ] One sentence above the marker says entries are appended oldest first by the `exercised.sh` script.
- [ ] The pull request creates `CHANGELOG.md` and changes no other file.
- [ ] `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass on the branch.

Two sibling cards created the places the record lives — the stamp in `README.md` and the log in `CHANGELOG.md`. Both were seeded by hand, and a record kept by hand stops being true the first time somebody forgets. This card adds the mechanism that keeps them true: `scripts/exercised.sh`, one small shell script that writes both files from one call, so an exercise of this repo ends with the repo saying so.

Usage is `scripts/exercised.sh <what> [date]` — `<date>` defaults to today's UTC calendar date. It replaces the single line between the README markers, and appends one entry to the end of the changelog log. It is idempotent: run twice with the same arguments, the second run leaves both files exactly as the first left them. If a marker is missing from either file it exits non-zero naming the file and the marker, and changes nothing.

The script resolves the repo root from its own location, overridable with the `EXERCISED_ROOT` environment variable — that override exists so the test can run the real script against a temporary copy of the two files rather than against the working tree.

Write the test first, then the script. `scripts/exercised.test.ts` is picked up by the existing `npm test` (vitest scans the repo root); it is deliberately outside `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, so do NOT add it there and do NOT add `@types/node` — `npm run typecheck` must keep passing untouched.

Do not edit `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `vite.config.ts`. This card adds two files under `scripts/` and nothing else; the two files it writes are written when the script RUNS, never in this pull request.

**Files: **`scripts/exercised.sh`, `scripts/exercised.test.ts`

## Contract — the exercise stamp

Written identically in this card, in DRE-3026 (`README.md`) and in DRE-3027
(`CHANGELOG.md`). One line format, spelled the same way everywhere:

```
Last exercised: <DATE> by <WHAT>
```

* `<DATE>` — the UTC calendar date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-09-04`).
* `<WHAT>` — a short single-line label naming what exercised the repo: a Linear
  card id such as `DRE-3019`, a workflow name, or the word `manual`.

Three marker comments, each on its own line, spelled exactly:

```
<!-- exercised:begin -->
<!-- exercised:end -->
<!-- exercised:log -->
```

* `README.md` holds exactly ONE stamp line, alone between `<!-- exercised:begin -->`
  and `<!-- exercised:end -->`.
* `CHANGELOG.md` holds the history: every entry is `- ` followed by the same
  stamp line, appended below `<!-- exercised:log -->`, oldest first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/exercised.sh` exists, is committed with the executable bit set, and accepts `<what>` plus an optional `<date>` that defaults to today's UTC calendar date.
- [ ] Running it rewrites the one line between the README markers to `Last exercised: <date> by <what>`, and appends `- Last exercised: <date> by <what>` as the last entry under `<!-- exercised:log -->` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [ ] Running it a second time with identical arguments leaves both files byte-identical to their state after the first run.
- [ ] A missing marker in either file makes it exit non-zero with a message naming the file and the marker, and neither file is modified.
- [ ] `scripts/exercised.test.ts` covers all four behaviours above by running the real script against a temporary copy, and `npm test` leaves the repo's own `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` unchanged.
- [ ] The test commit precedes the script commit in the branch's history.
- [ ] The pull request adds `scripts/exercised.sh` and `scripts/exercised.test.ts` and changes no other file.
- [ ] `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass on the branch.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3026, DRE-3027

Three merged pull requests prove that code was written. They do not prove the repo can say when it was last exercised — the stamp and the log entry those cards left behind were both typed by an agent, and the script that is supposed to write them has never been run against anything real.

This card closes that gap. Once DRE-3026, DRE-3027 and DRE-3028 have merged, an operator takes a fresh checkout of `main` and runs the real script against the live repo, watching what it does to the two files. The observation is then recorded in the repo so it merges rather than evaporating: a short note carrying the exact command, the date it ran, the two files before and after, and what the second run did.

The record is the deliverable, and the stamp on `main` afterwards is the evidence: written by the mechanism, on a date nobody chose, naming the run that caused it.

**Files: **`docs/proof-DRE-3019.md` (the observation), plus whatever `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` the script itself rewrites during the run — those two are never edited by a person on this card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After DRE-3026, DRE-3027 and DRE-3028 have merged, an operator runs `./exercised.sh DRE-3019` by hand from the repo's `scripts` directory on a fresh checkout of `main`, against the live repo.
- [ ] The observation is recorded in `docs/proof-DRE-3019.md` and merged to `main`: the command, the date and time it ran, the `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` lines before and after, and the exit status.
- [ ] A second run with the same arguments is performed by hand in the same session, and the note records that it changed nothing.
- [ ] On `main` afterwards, the README stamp line and the last changelog entry both read the date the script actually ran and `DRE-3019` as the label, and neither line was typed by a person.
- [ ] If any step fails, the note records what happened instead — a failed proof is recorded, never quietly retried until it passes.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3026, DRE-3027, DRE-3028

A merged pull request and a green test suite are invisible to the person who green-lit this epic. This card is how the CEO sees the result, in the place he would naturally look: the demo repo's front page.

An operator opens the repo on GitHub, where the rendered `README.md` now carries a `## Last exercised` section showing a real date and a real label, and captures it. The same capture takes in the last few entries of `CHANGELOG.md`, which is the part that answers the second question — not just when, but how often, and whether the sandbox is alive or abandoned.

Post both captures to DRE-3019 as a comment with one plain-English sentence saying what a reader now learns from the repo without opening any code. No file in this repo changes on this card.

**Files:** none — nothing is committed by this card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An operator opens the demo repo's rendered README on GitHub by hand and captures the `## Last exercised` section showing a real date and a real label.
- [ ] The same operator captures the last three entries of the changelog.
- [ ] A comment on DRE-3019 carries both captures plus one plain-English sentence — no code, no file paths — saying what the repo now tells a reader.
- [ ] The CEO can answer "when was this repo last exercised, and by what" from that comment alone.
- [ ] No file in the repo is changed by this card.

**Blocked by:** DRE-3026, DRE-3027, DRE-3028, DRE-3031
